MemGPT divides main context into three parts: read-only system instructions, a fixed-size working context that only function calls can write, and a FIFO message queue. https://arxiv.org/html/2310.08560 30. In MemGPT, the queue manager sends a "memory pressure" warning at 70% of the context window. The warning prompts the model to save important information. https://arxiv.org/html/2310.08560 31. At 100% of the window, MemGPT flushes about 50% of the context. The evicted messages go into a new recursive summary built from the old summary. That summary sits at the head of the FIFO queue. http

11. MemGPT (2023) set up two thresholds. A "warning token count" (e.g. 70% of the window) triggers a memory-pressure warning so the model can save important facts first. A "flush token count" (e.g. 100%) evicts messages (e.g. 50% of the window) and folds them into a recursive summary. https://arxiv.org/html/2310.08560 12. MemGPT keeps evicted messages "indefinitely in recall storage," readable through function calls. Its compaction is therefore restorable, not destructive. https://arxiv.org/html/2310.08560 13. **In scope.** This report covers two linked things. The first is context-window pressure: why a model's use of its context gets worse as the context grows, and the hard limits of the window. The second is compaction: the operations that shrink an agent's working context. These are summarizing old turns, clearing old tool results, evicting from a FIFO queue with a recursive summary, and producing an opaque compacted state. The report covers their triggers, invariants, failure modes, and measured trade-offs.

**In scope:** how long context degrades model behavior (pressure) and how agents shrink context mid-task (compaction: summarization, tool-result clearing, observation masking, server-side compaction). This report covers only boundary conditions, failure modes, disagreements, and disconfirming evidence.

**In scope.** Two linked ideas: - **Context-window pressure.** Model quality falls, and cost rises, as the context window fills. - **Compaction.** An agent or API responds to that pressure by summarizing, clearing, or evicting older context so the work can continue.

**In scope:** what "context-window pressure" is (quality and cost loss as a live context fills), and the operational techniques that relieve it inside one agent run: summarizing compaction, tool-result clearing or observation masking, thinking-block clearing, context resets with handoff artifacts, and pressure signals (thresholds, budget awareness). Also covered: their trade-offs, how to evaluate them, and concrete API-level implications.
